extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer-review researchers, biomedical researchers, and meta-researchers studying editorial processes
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials assessing interventions designed to improve the quality, speed, or outcomes of peer review in biomedical journals. Includes methods for study selection, outcome measurement, bias assessment, and data synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention category: Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Training, which included training or mentoring programs for peer reviewers to provide instructional support for appropriately evaluating important components of manuscript submissions. These interventions directly target the ability of peer reviewers to appropriately evaluate the quality of the manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include structured workshops with journal editors, self-taught training packages, mentoring where new reviewers discuss reviews with senior reviewers, and feedback (editors' ratings provided to reviewers). RCTs compared these to the usual process; heterogeneity across training types should be expected when pooling results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention category: Addition of specific-expertise peer reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Addition of peer reviewers for specific tasks or with specific expertise such as adding a statistical peer reviewer, whose main task is to detect the misuse of methods or misreporting of statistical analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by randomizing manuscripts or reviewer assignment to include an extra specialist reviewer (e.g., statistician) versus usual review; reported to improve final manuscript quality in the included RCTs (SMD reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention category: Use of a checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers’ use of a checklist, such as reporting guideline checklists, to evaluate the quality of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklists evaluated included reporting-guideline based items (e.g., CONSORT-derived). Trials measured impact on final manuscript quality; pooling must account for which checklist and how it was implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention category: Open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: “Open” peer review process, whereby peer reviewers are informed that their name would be revealed to the authors, other peer reviewers, and/or the public. The purpose is to increase transparency and accountability of reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trials varied in intensity (open to other reviewers, open to authors, public posting). Subgroup analyses by intensity recommended. Reported effects include small improvement in peer review report quality and reductions in rejection recommendations; potential effects on review time should be measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention category: Blinded (masked) peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: “Blinded”/masked peer review, whereby peer reviewers are blinded to author names and affiliation. Author names and/or identifying credentials are removed from manuscripts sent for peer review to remove or minimize bias from author identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blinding aims to favor objectivity/fairness; measured outcomes in trials included peer review report quality and rejection rate. Note: blinding participants/providers often impossible; detection bias and assessment of fairness are difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention category: Other interventions to accelerate review
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other types of interventions identified aimed at increasing the speed of the peer review process (e.g., asking referees if they agree before sending manuscript, phone calls to reviewers, early editorial screening).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interventions to improve speed were heterogeneous; trials report time-to-decision or overall duration. Outcomes were variably reported and often could not be meta-analysed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final manuscript quality (outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final manuscript quality (i.e., revised manuscript after all peer review assessments and rounds). Several scales were used to assess manuscript quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly measured with the Manuscript Quality Assessment Instrument (MQAI) — a 34-item scale (items scored 1–5) organized by article sections (Title/Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions, General evaluation). Other scales measured completeness of reporting (e.g., CONSORT-based items). High score indicates higher manuscript quality. Use SMD when pooling because different scales were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the peer review report (outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the peer review report, measured by scales such as the Review Quality Instrument (RQI) or editors' routine quality rating scales. A high score indicates a high quality peer review report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RQI (latest version) is an eight-item scale: importance, originality, methodology, presentation, constructiveness of comments, substantiation of comments and interpretation of results, plus a global item; each item scored 1–5. Report inter-rater reliability (kappa) and use SMD to pool across different versions/scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection rate (outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection rate, defined as the recommendation by peer reviewers about whether or not the reviewed manuscripts should be rejected from publication in the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a binary outcome (recommend reject vs not). Use odds ratios for meta-analysis. Interpretation must consider that rejection recommendations may reflect manuscript quality, topic interest, or reviewer/editor subjectivity; association between rejection recommendations and actual study quality not necessarily established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time spent on the peer review (outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time spent on the peer review as reported by peer reviewers. Important to evaluate burden and possible cost of the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as mean (and SD) per arm; use mean differences for pooling. Time may increase with some interventions (e.g., open review) and should be reported to assess trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall duration of the peer review process (outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall duration of the peer review process (e.g., time to manuscript decision or overall time for peer review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured at manuscript-level; useful for assessing interventions aimed at accelerating editorial workflow. Reporting completeness varies across trials; unsuitable reporting may preclude meta-analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion criteria for studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Include randomized controlled trials (RCTs), whatever the unit of randomization (manuscript or peer reviewers), evaluating any interventions aimed at improving the quality of peer review for biomedical publications. Exclude RCTs evaluating the presence and effect of peer reviewer bias on the outcome (such as positive outcome bias) and non-randomized studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No language or date limits. Collate duplicate publications for unique trials. Define 'biomedical research' scope explicitly. Use trial registry searches and hand-search references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment domains (Cochrane tool)
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk-of-bias domains assessed: selection bias (random sequence generation and allocation concealment), detection bias (blinding of outcome assessors), and attrition bias (incomplete outcome data). Performance bias (blinding of participants and providers) was not assessed because blinding was generally impossible in this context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate each domain as low, high or unclear risk according to Cochrane guidelines. Assess blinding and incomplete outcome data at the outcome level. Consider detection bias low when reviewers not aware of study hypothesis or assessed outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data extraction and reviewer independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Data extraction performed independently by two researchers using a standardized data extraction form; disagreements resolved by discussion and, if needed, a third reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract general study characteristics, unit of randomization, eligibility criteria, numbers randomized/analyzed, interventions, and risk-of-bias judgments. When assessment differed, discuss to consensus; use third reviewer if necessary. Contact study authors for unclear risk or missing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome selection rule to avoid selective inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: When several results were reported for selected outcomes (e.g., several scales or time points), retrieve results for the outcome reported as the primary outcome in the manuscript or the final/latest time of assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify outcomes; use final/latest assessment to ensure consistency; avoid mixing change-from-baseline and final-value scores improperly when computing SMDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical synthesis standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment effect measures: odds ratios for binary outcomes and standardized mean differences for continuous outcomes when different scales used. Use random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian and Laird) due to diversity of interventions and settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess heterogeneity with forest plots, Cochrane's Q test, and I2 statistic. Perform subgroup analyses where prespecified (e.g., intensity of open peer review). Use Review Manager and follow Cochrane Handbook recommendations for computing/deriving means and SDs when not reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multi-arm trials and multiple intervention groups
rubrics_metrics.description: For studies with multiple intervention groups, follow Cochrane recommendations: combine relevant intervention groups into a single group, combine control groups, or select one pair of interventions and exclude others when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should be made a priori where possible; document which arms were combined or excluded and why. Do not pool incompatible comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement derivation and data retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: When outcome data not reported as mean and SD, derive these from reported data following Cochrane Handbook recommendations; extract data from published figures using digitizing software when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record methods used for derivation, contact authors for missing data, and report any assumptions. Use DigitizeIt (or equivalent) for figure extraction and follow Cochrane guidance on conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and interpretation of specific measurement instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript and review quality instruments (e.g., MQAI, RQI, editors' routine quality scales) have defined items and scoring systems; a high score indicates higher quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document which instrument/version was used, its items and psychometric properties (e.g., inter-rater reliability, kappa). Acknowledge limitations: MQAI measures reporting completeness not the research quality itself; editors' routine scales may have uncertain validity.
